parent.reason: The parent question conflates (1) what each inventoried document establishes and (2) which document governs on disagreement. Workspace text supports mechanically partitionable answers by document_kind and incorporation pattern: issued permits self-define governing Parts; appendices are incorporated by cross-reference; supporting package documents frame draft/proposed rationale and defer limitations. Filename kind is not hierarchy. A one-size parent admission would over-generalize or leave minor_modification authority unresolved. Children supersede the coarse parent.

plan.proposition: Without ranking from filenames, what do inventoried permit documents establish, and which document governs if they disagree?
would_establish: Issued final_permit cover pages define a self-contained governing corpus (named Parts I–III/IV) as the authorization to discharge.
Part II appendices and Farmington Part IV are incorporated into the issued permit by internal cross-reference, not independent binding authority.
Fact sheets, statements of basis, and reasonable-potential files establish draft/proposed explanatory package material and defer enforceable limitations to the permit.
Inventory document_kind labels are not a reliable precedence hierarchy; document text must govern classification and authority.
No workspace text states an explicit inter-document 'in the event of conflict' precedence clause across all package file types.
would_refute: Filename or inventory document_kind alone determines binding authority or conflict precedence (e.g., final_permit > fact_sheet > reasonable_potential).
All twelve inventoried files are independently co-equal binding authorization documents with no functional precedence.
Precedence is wholly unknowable without an explicit named conflict clause (issued-permit self-definition and supporting-document draft framing still establish functional precedence).
insufficient_alone: document_inventory.json provides kind labels, permit association, and hashes but no incorporation, precedence, or narrative authority metadata.
PRIOR_PACKET.json is a bounded prior retrieval packet, not source-established disposition.
Absence of an explicit conflict clause does not prove co-equal authority when issued permits self-define governing parts and supporting documents frame content as draft/proposed.
Training-data or general NPDES practice is not workspace evidence for this obligation.
